title: Reduce query fanout with skyline approximation and read-through microcache
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Some dashboard queries fan out to many tenant shards which causes high tail latency and spikes in read throughput on the analytics pipeline. This ticket proposes a dual approach: (1) a lightweight skyline-approximation layer that picks a small, high-value subset of shards to query based on recent time-decayed metrics and query selectivity heuristics, and (2) a read-through microcache (tenant+query-hash keyed) that caches aggregated partial results for short staleness windows. The goal is to reduce average and 95th/99th percentile latencies and smooth downstream pipeline load without sacrificing accuracy beyond a bounded staleness/recall budget.
design_summary: We will add an inline 'candidate-selection' stage to the Console query service before issuing fanout reads. Candidate-selection uses compact telemetry vectors (recent per-shard hit-rate, avg-response-latency, cardinality-estimate) and a skyline-approximation greedy routine to return N shards (configurable per-route). The microcache is an LRU store with per-key TTL and optional Bloom-filtered negative cache for very selective queries. On cache-miss, the service issues the reduced fanout and populates the microcache asynchronously while returning the combined response.
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs latency: skyline-approx favors high-recall shards but may drop low-significance shards causing small recall loss; we bound this with per-route recall targets.
Staleness vs cost: microcache TTL reduces backend load but introduces bounded staleness; set default TTL to 30s and allow route override.
Complexity: candidate-selection adds CPU work per-request; mitigate by compact telemetry and sampling.
Operational: telemetry correctness required; if telemetry stream is delayed, fallback to full fanout to avoid data loss.
Cache consistency: writes/rollups that change underlying data may require cache invalidation; plan to emit simple invalidation events per-tenant-route to the cache topic.
Edge cases: very low-cardinality tenants should bypass skyline and use full fanout to ensure correctness.
implementation_tasks: Add candidate-selection module in console-query service (golang): telemetry ingestion, skyline-approx algorithm, config knobs.
Implement read-through microcache service (redis-compatible or in-process memcache fallback) with tenant+route+query-hash keys and negative Bloom filter support.
Instrument metrics: candidate_count, skipped_shards, recall_estimate, cache_hit_rate, cache_populate_latency, end_to_end_p95/p99.
Create rollout plan: 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% with per-tenant opt-out; add canary routes for critical customers.
Add cache invalidation producer on the analytics ETL job when materialized aggregates update.
E2E tests: synthetic workloads with varying shard hotness and selectivity to measure recall and latency.
Docs: update Console routing and rollout pages describing staleness guarantees and opt-out.
Create an incident playbook for skyline-selection regressions (how to force full fanout via runtime flag).
Performance budget: candidate-selection should add <2ms median overhead and reduce downstream read ops by >=40% for heavy-fanout queries.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end latency for targeted dashboard routes reduced by >=25% under synthetic fanout workload.
Downstream analytics read ops reduced by >=35% for the measured heavy queries.
Recall loss <=1% (or configurable route threshold) compared to full-fanout baseline on representative datasets.
Cache hit rate >=20% for steady-state traffic after 10 minutes warmup in canary.
Operational metrics and dashboards are added and firing alerts for abnormal candidate-selection drop rates or telemetry freshness.
Rollout can be fully disabled via runtime config without requiring deploy.
Technical design doc and runbook merged and reviewed by infra and analytics owners.
